title: First 7 days
summary: Land, sleep, get a +65 number, and start pass issuance. Keep the list short so the jet lag does not win — Singpass and a proper bank account usually wait for biometrics. Dependency map: /guides/first-week-sim-singpass-bank.

items.title: Submit SG Arrival Card before landing
items.detail: ICA requires the free SG Arrival Card (with electronic health declaration) within three days before arrival, including the day you land — via the e-Service or MyICA app. Keep your IPA or pass letter ready at immigration. If you are still overseas, finish the pre-arrival playbook first.

items.title: Confirm pre-arrival pack is done (IPA, meds, cash bridge)
items.detail: HSA approvals, shipping triage, and the foreign-card cash bridge should already be closed before Changi. Use /journeys/pre-arrival if anything is still open.

items.title: Choose Grab vs taxi vs MRT from Changi
items.detail: Compare Grab’s upfront fare with a metered taxi plus LTA’s Changi location surcharge (S$8 from 5pm–11:59pm, else S$6). MRT only with light bags. Card in Grab beats hunting SGD cash.

items.title: Get a prepaid +65 SIM or eSIM with passport
items.detail: Changi and mall kiosks sell prepaid SIMs on passport alone. Postpaid often wants a physical pass or stable address. You need a Singapore number for HR/MOM contact updates, banking OTPs, and Singpass SMS 2FA later.

items.title: Confirm HSA medication approvals are printed or on phone
items.detail: Controlled ADHD / sleep / anxiety meds need prior HSA approval (apply ≥2 weeks out). Keep approval email + prescription + original packs ready if ICA asks. Non-controlled personal meds: up to 3 months in labelled containers.

items.title: Do not bring vaporisers — illegal for visitors and pass holders
items.detail: E-vaporisers are prohibited. Devices are seized; foreigners face composition fines and pass-revocation risk on repeat or etomidate (K-pod) cases. Not covered by HSA personal-medication rules.

items.title: Confirm temporary housing keys and Wi-Fi
items.detail: Serviced apartment, hotel, or host address — note gate access codes, visitor policy, and a postal address HR can use for pass-card delivery.

items.title: Message HR / relocation — issuance and biometrics
items.detail: Confirm pass issuance timing, any medical still pending, and the Employment Pass Services Centre (EPSC) biometrics appointment. After issuance you typically get a Notification Letter that lets you work while the card is printed — verify the live MOM window with HR.

items.title: Install SGWorkPass after EPSC / issuance
items.detail: Once Singpass is registered at EPSC (or after document verification), open SGWorkPass and confirm your digital work pass shows. Photograph the FIN — banks and telcos ask for it before the plastic card arrives. If the plastic is lost later, HR must file MOM replacement within one week — digital pass does not waive that.

items.title: Install ScamShield and save helpline 1799
items.detail: New FIN / Singpass holders are prime phishing targets. Install ScamShield, grant call/SMS filters, and memorise: banks and government never ask you on WhatsApp to transfer money or share OTPs. Overseas helpline: +65 6869 1799.

items.title: Load SimplyGo / contactless transit + bridge cash
items.detail: Foreign contactless works day one (SimplyGo S$0.60/day admin fee). Or buy an EZ-Link. Keep a foreign-card or remittance bridge until the local salary account opens — full banking belongs on the 30-day list.

items.title: Locate a nearby GP clinic
items.detail: Save one private panel GP or polyclinic within a short walk or bus of where you are sleeping. Jet lag plus humidity is a classic first-week combo — know 995 vs GP triage.

items.title: Do a small grocery and hawker recon
items.detail: Cold drinks, fruit, and one neighbourhood hawker centre. You do not need to master Singapore cuisine on day two.
